With that bot token securely loaded into `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, the commands are:

```sh
slack api auth.test
slack api conversations.info channel=D0C6F49F2KD
slack api conversations.replies channel=D0C6F49F2KD ts=ROOT_TIMESTAMP limit=200
```

The last command retrieves the parent and replies; continue with `cursor=...` when `response_metadata.next_cursor` is nonempty. [Slack thread API](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.replies/)

**Reading yyovil’s DM through Clanker is different from authenticating as yyovil.** If you specifically require yyovil’s identity, use yyovil’s authorized user token and require `auth.test.user_id` to equal `U0C6M6DMWAW`. `--team` only selects the workspace. Also, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` takes priority over `SLACK_USER_TOKEN`, so don’t leave it set when selecting a user token. [Identity verification](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/auth.test/)

The draft’s Slack-thread-to-Kernel-browser mapping is source-supported.

Add one clarification for login issues: `kernel_auth_flows.connection_id` identifies a **Managed Auth connection**, not a browser session. Its `request_id` and `profile_name` also cannot be passed to `kernel browsers ...`. Managed Auth shares the verified `team/requester/home/thread` correlation tuple but needs its own confirmed CLI resource lookup. See [managed_auth.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/managed_auth.py:31).

Browser telemetry should supplement the matching Hermes `messages.tool_calls`, `tool_name`, and `content`; telemetry alone does not prove a tool’s action or website acceptance. See [hermes_state_common.py](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/hermes/hermes_state_common.py:402).

No other material correction found.
